newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lehman hopeful positive progress in Minmetals case.
newsitem.headline: Lehman hopeful positive progress in Minmetals case.

text.p: Lehman Brothers said on Tuesday it was hopeful of positive development in its lawsuit against China's state-owned Minmetals International Non-Ferrous Metals Trading Co, in which it had said it wanted a settlement.
"We remain very hopeful of perhaps somthing positive developing on the Minmetals case," Lehman Brothers Asia Ltd managing director Stephen Taran told a news conference.
He noted the firm had already reached settlement with two other Chinese companies in separate lawsuits.
Lehman's China business had not be affected by the Minmetals lawsuit, Taran said.
"Our business has not been affected by the legal difficulties that we had with specific companies," he said.

In 1994, Lehman filed a US$53 million suit against Minmetals and its parent. It claimed that Minmetals had reneged on foreign exchange and swap transactions after incurring losses, and that its parent had guaranteed the subsidiary's losses.
Minmetals subsequently filed a US$128 million countersuit against Lehman, including six counter claims of fraud alleging Lehman knew the investments were unsuitable for it.
